title: DSP Y: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
abstract: DSPy is a programming model that translates prompting techniques into parameterized declarative modules and introduces an effective compiler with general optimization strategies to optimize arbitrary pipelines of these modules. With DSPy, we can implement very short programs that can bootstrap self-improving multi-stage NLP systems using LMs as small as llama2-13b-chat and T5-Large.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You'd break it down into smaller, manageable steps. That's what DSPy does for language models (LMs). It takes complex tasks and decomposes them into smaller, more manageable LM calls.

This approach allows for more systematic development and optimization of LM pipelines, making it easier to build high-performing NLP systems.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
DSPy programs are expressed in Python, using natural language signatures to assign work to the LM. These signatures are then compiled into self-improving and pipeline-adaptive prompts or finetunes.

The DSPy compiler optimizes any DSPy program to improve quality or cost, using teleprompters to determine how the modules should learn from data.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Our evaluations show that DSPy programs outperform systems using hand-crafted prompts, while also allowing our programs to use much smaller and hence more efficient LMs effectively.

For example, on the GSM8K math word problems task, DSPy improves GPT-3.5 from 24.0% to 62.7% accuracy and Llama2-13b-chat from 7.0% to 39.0% accuracy.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
DSPy has the potential to revolutionize the way we build NLP systems. By providing a systematic approach to developing and optimizing LM pipelines, DSPy can reduce the role of artful prompt construction in modern AI.

This can lead to more efficient and effective NLP systems, and enable the development of new modular, composable programs and optimizers.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
DSPy introduces several key innovations, including the use of natural language signatures, parameterized declarative modules, and teleprompters.

These innovations enable the development of self-improving pipelines that can adapt to different LMs and tasks, and can outperform expert-written prompts.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
DSPy is available on GitHub, and can be used to build and optimize your own NLP systems.

Try using DSPy to improve the performance of your favorite LM on a task of your choice, and see the benefits of self-improving pipelines for yourself.
